findings.claim: Inverted condition in the second hunk set: `if (stringMembers.ContainsKey(member.StringKey)) { stringMembers.Add(...) }` is the opposite of the sibling code. Add only runs when the key already exists, so it throws ArgumentException on duplicates. New string keys are never added, so members are silently dropped from the collected ObjectSerializationInfo. The generator/analyzer can crash on duplicate string keys, and generated formatters can omit members, so those fields are not serialized or deserialized. This is a correctness defect with a limited security effect: an unhandled generator exception disables analyzer diagnostics.

receipt_plan.detail: Run a generator/analyzer test on a [MessagePackObject] type with string-key members, including a public property with [Key("a")]. Expect a formatter containing the member, and no exception for duplicate string keys. With the inverted ContainsKey, the member is missing from the output, and a duplicate key throws ArgumentException.
